results.evidence: SOW Section 1.2: "For purposes of this SOW, "Client Germplasm" means seed physically delivered to Provider by or on behalf of Client under Section 3 of this SOW." SOW Section 7.1: "Provider's obligations under Sections 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4 of the MSA, and its obligations of confidentiality under Section 8 of the MSA, apply in respect of the Services under this SOW to Client Germplasm."
results.reason: The MSA defines Client Germplasm broadly: seed, lines, tissue, DNA and all genotypic data derived from them. The SOW redefines it for this SOW as delivered seed only. Under MSA 2.3 the SOW prevails for its own Services. SOW 7.1 then ties Padouth's use restriction, segregated storage, return/destruction and confidentiality duties to that narrow term. As a result, the tissue, extracted DNA and raw marker and genotype data Padouth generates from Stukand's elite inbreds are no longer clearly covered. Those duties are Padouth's, so the gap hurts Stukand: Padouth could argue it may keep and use that material and data. MSA 8.1 still treats Deliverables as Client confidential information and MSA 7.2 vests Deliverables in Client. But that protection reaches only the delivered files, not undelivered raw data, DNA or tissue. It also does not restore the MSA 4.2 no-use or 4.4 return/destruction duties for those items. Nothing in the folder cures or expressly limits the narrowing. The SOW is the operative program document, and its signature blocks are blank, so Stukand can still fix the definition. The point is actionable.

results.evidence: "Provider may assign this Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, without Client's consent, to any Affiliate or to any successor or acquirer of all or part of its business."
results.reason: Section 15.2 is one-sided. Stukand (Client) needs Padouth's consent to assign, and Section 15.3 adds a change-of-control trigger against Stukand. Padouth (Provider) can assign freely, including a partial assignment to a buyer of any part of its business, such as a competing seed company. Nothing in the documents cures this. Section 4.2 limits the assignee's use of the germplasm, but the assignee would still hold Stukand's germplasm and confidential data as a permitted assign (Sections 8.2 and 15.1). Term Sheet Section 7.1 provided for mutual consent, but that term sheet is non-binding and MSA Section 2.3 makes the MSA prevail. SOW No. 1 does not change this. Neither does its narrowed definition of Client Germplasm; if anything, that narrowing weakens Stukand's protection over derived data. The issue remains actionable: the MSA is ongoing, Padouth has not assigned, and Stukand can seek an amendment under Section 18.3, for example during the consent discussions it will need with Padouth for its pending Varnell change of control.

results.evidence: SOW Section 9.4: "Section 10.3(c) of the MSA shall not apply to the Services under this SOW. All liability of either Party arising out of or relating to the Services under this SOW is subject to the cap in Section 10.2 of the MSA."
results.reason: MSA 10.3(c) takes Provider's misuse or misappropriation of Client Germplasm outside the 12-month-fees cap and the indirect-damages exclusion. SOW 9.4 switches that carve-out off for this program. Its second sentence then puts all liability under the cap, which may also swallow the confidentiality carve-out in 10.3(b) even though SOW 7.1 imports MSA Section 8. Under MSA 2.3 the SOW prevails for its own Services. So Padouth's liability for misappropriating or misusing Stukand's elite inbred source populations and DH Lines is limited to about twelve months of fees. That is roughly $1.17M at most, and less early in the program. Lost-profit damages would also be excluded under 10.1. The SOW also narrows 'Client Germplasm' (1.2) to seed physically delivered, so derived DH Lines, tissue and genotype data lose some of the germplasm protections. The obligation and the liability sit with Provider, so the restriction hurts only Stukand. Nothing in the folder cures it. The SOW signature blocks are blank, so this can still be negotiated, or if signed, an amendment can be pursued. The issue is real and actionable.

results.evidence: MSA Section 15.3: "Any direct or indirect change of control of Client, including a change of control of any parent entity of Client, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise, shall be deemed an assignment requiring Provider's prior written consent. If such a change of control occurs without Provider's prior written consent, Provider may terminate this Agreement and any or all SOWs on written notice to Client and retain all Fees prepaid under any SOW." SOW No. 1 Recital B: "On May 4, 2026, Stukand Holdings Corp., the parent company of Client, entered into a stock purchase agreement with Varnell AgriSciences, Inc. ... The transaction is expected to close on or about December 15, 2026."
results.reason: The obligation falls on Stukand, the client. It needs Padouth's consent, and Padouth holds the termination and fee-retention remedy. The Varnell acquisition of Stukand's parent is an indirect change of control that 15.3 expressly covers. Nothing in the folder records Padouth's consent or a waiver. SOW No. 1 notes the deal in a recital but does not carve it out or record any consent. Stukand has a $300,000 mobilization payment at stake, and the DH program runs past the December 15, 2026 closing (D0 transplant is due December 18, 2026). The deal has not closed as of today (November 10, 2026), so Stukand can still get consent before closing. The provision is also one-sided and departs from the term sheet's mutual consent concept. The issue is present and still actionable.

results.evidence: SOW Section 12.1: "This SOW, and any dispute arising out of or relating to the Services under this SOW, are governed by the laws of the State of Iowa, without regard to its conflict of laws principles." SOW Section 12.2: "Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in Polk County, Iowa, and of the federal courts for the district that includes Polk County..." MSA Section 17.1 says the MSA "and each SOW" are governed by New York law. MSA Section 17.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts. MSA Section 2.3: "An SOW prevails over the MSA only for its own Services."
results.reason: The SOW and the MSA each choose a different governing law and a different exclusive forum. Under MSA Section 2.3, the SOW's Iowa/Polk County clause controls disputes over the doubled-haploid Services. Claims that arise under the MSA itself would stay under New York law in New York County. That includes germplasm misuse under MSA Section 4, confidentiality under Section 8, indemnity under Section 11, and termination on change of control under Section 15.3, which is live given the pending Varnell acquisition. One dispute with Padouth could therefore split between two forums with competing exclusive-jurisdiction clauses. That invites parallel proceedings, arguments over which forum controls, and inconsistent results. Stukand is based in Ames, so Iowa may look convenient. But nothing in the documents shows the split was intended or reconciled. There is no carve-out, no statement that the SOW clause overrides MSA Section 17 for all related claims, and no coordination mechanism. The SOW signature blocks are blank, and nothing shows Stukand accepted the split. The problem is still actionable: Stukand can conform Section 12 to the MSA or amend both documents to choose a single law and forum.
